candidates.attacker_control: ZIP entry names and comments are arbitrary Strings supplied by the application: ZipArchiveEntry constructors/setName/setComment, ZipArchiveOutputStream.setComment, or raw-entry copying (addRawArchiveEntry, used by ScatterZipOutputStream/ChangeSet workflows). An attacker who can influence such a string can supply one ending in an unpaired high surrogate, e.g. a JSON value containing the escape \uD800, truncated surrogate pairs produced by string slicing of untrusted text, or malformed names from external metadata. No validation of the name/comment occurs before encoding.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified in source that canEncode() is evaluated first but does not prevent the sink: for UTF-8 (useReplacement=true) canEncode may return true or false, and both getEntryEncoding branches still yield the UTF-8 NioZipEncoding for the default/fallback configurations, so encode() is called either way. Checked the alternative UNMAPPABLE behavior for non-UTF-8 REPORT encoders (single-byte charsets return unmappable and the existing branch consumes the character, so the hang is charset-dependent — but the default is UTF-8 and fallbackToUTF8 funnels non-encodable names to UTF8_ZIP_ENCODING). Confirmed there is no isUnderflow handling in any main source file (repo-wide search) and that the loop mutates no state when UNDERFLOW is returned. Checked for an earlier guard/normalization of names (none in ZipArchiveEntry/putArchiveEntry). Could not execute code, so the JDK CharsetEncoder UNDERFLOW-with-unconsumed-incomplete-sequence behavior is established from its documented contract plus the code's own comment at NioZipEncoding.java:117-119 ('tell the encoder we are done... may have caused underflow, but that's been ignored traditionally'), not from runtime confirmation.
candidates.impact: Availability loss / denial of service: the calling thread (e.g. a request-handling thread of a service that packages user-controlled names into a ZIP) spins in a tight loop at full CPU indefinitely; no IOException is raised, the archive is never finished, and the thread/process must be killed. In multi-tenant or network-facing services this is a remotely triggerable hang.
candidates.prerequisites: 1) The application writes a ZIP through ZipArchiveOutputStream (directly, or via ScatterZipOutputStream/archiver/ChangeSet copy paths) with a name or comment derived from untrusted input. 2) The name/comment ends with an unpaired high surrogate. 3) The encoding used is UTF-8 — the class default (DEFAULT_ENCODING = ZipEncodingHelper.UTF8 at line 136 and the field at 225-226) — or fallbackToUTF8 is enabled so the shared UTF8_ZIP_ENCODING is used, or the platform default charset is UTF-8 (isUTF8 -> useReplacement=true). With a configured single-byte charset and fallbackToUTF8=false the trailing surrogate is UNMAPPABLE and is consumed via the %Uxxxx branch, so that specific configuration does not hang.
candidates.root_cause: NioZipEncoding.encode(String) loops with `while (cb.remaining() > 0)` and calls `enc.encode(cb, out, false)` (endOfInput=false). It handles only MALFORMED/UNMAPPABLE (writes %Uxxxx escapes and consumes characters via cb.get()) and OVERFLOW (grows the output buffer). It has no branch for UNDERFLOW. The JDK CharsetEncoder contract states that with endOfInput=false an incomplete trailing character sequence is left in the input buffer and UNDERFLOW is returned. Therefore an input whose last character is an unpaired high surrogate (e.g. "name\uD800") produces UNDERFLOW with cb.remaining() > 0 and zero progress on every iteration: no output, no exception, no state change, so the loop spins forever. (A search of main sources shows no isUnderflow handling anywhere; the same unguarded pattern also exists in the private encodeFully helper, lines 136-146, though its input is an ASCII escape sequence.)
candidates.title: Infinite loop (CPU exhaustion DoS) in NioZipEncoding.encode for names/comments ending in an unpaired high surrogate
candidates.trace: putArchiveEntry(ArchiveEntry) (ZipArchiveOutputStream.java:726/742) -> writeLocalFileHeader(ze, phased) (line 787, method at 1031-1033: `zipEncoding.canEncode(ze.getName())` then `getName(ze)`) -> getName (1594-1596: `getEntryEncoding(ze).encode(ze.getName())`) -> getEntryEncoding (1588-1592: returns ZipEncodingHelper.UTF8_ZIP_ENCODING when !encodable && fallbackToUTF8, otherwise the configured encoding, default UTF-8) -> NioZipEncoding.encode (NioZipEncoding.java:77) -> newEncoder() (161-172, UTF-8 uses REPLACE; others use REPORT) -> loop at 85-116 calls `enc.encode(cb, out, false)` at 86; when the trailing high surrogate is unconsumed, result is UNDERFLOW, which matches neither `res.isUnmappable()/isMalformed()` (88) nor `res.isOverflow()` (112), so the while condition remains true forever. The same encode() sink is also reached for entry comments (line 1161 via addUnicodeExtraFields, line 1246 in the central directory) and for the archive-level comment in finish() (line 1383).
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed: the exact JDK behavior (UNDERFLOW leaving the trailing high surrogate in the buffer, no progress) was reasoned from the CharsetEncoder contract and source, not executed. The precise set of configurations that reach the hang (UTF-8 default; fallbackToUTF8=true; platform default UTF-8) is derived by source reading and could vary with JDK encoder internals. No claim is made that this maps to a specific CVE/ground-truth patch; exposure in a given application depends on it feeding attacker-influenced names/comments to a ZIP writer.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-835 Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop') — denial of service

coverage_summary: Scope: 424 model-visible files under src/main and src/test (360 Java, 1 sensitive-name file excluded, binary-like files skipped by the tooling; the P1 index additionally reports only 127 files parsed and 194 omitted, with no control-flow/data-flow/semantic resolution and only syntax/navigation edges). I read the ZIP write/encode path end to end (NioZipEncoding, ZipEncodingHelper, ZipArchiveOutputStream name/comment/central-directory/raw-copy paths, CharsetAccessor/ZipEncoding interface, NioZipEncodingTest-relevant tests), the 7z reader/writer name handling, tar name/PAX handling, cpio/dump/ar/arj name decoding, and the 7z/zip compressor entry points; I used the relation index only to locate declarations/callers and verified each relevant edge in source text. I did not read every compressor decoder or every test file line-by-line.
limitations: No code execution, tests, scanners, or exploit payloads; the infinite loop is not runtime-confirmed. The UNDERFLOW-with-unconsumed-incomplete-sequence behavior of java.nio.charset.CharsetEncoder.encode(..., false) is inferred from its documented contract and the code's own comments, not observed.
P1 index is partial: only 127 of 424 files parsed, 194 omitted, and it supports no control-flow or data flow, so reachability was established by manual source tracing only for the paths cited.
Only source evidence was used; no fix commit, CVE mapping, sibling condition, or ground-truth data was consulted, so the historical vulnerability identity is not verified.
Attacker control over entry names/comments depends on the integrating application (e.g. untrusted names forming archive entries); the library itself does not accept networked input directly.
Not all 360 Java files were reviewed exhaustively; areas not examined in depth include most compressor codecs, bzip2/BlockSort internals, docs/build files, and the bulk of the test suite.

rejected_leads.lead: SevenZFile kName (file names) parsing could hang/overflow on malformed name blocks
rejected_leads.reason: Inspected SevenZFile.java:898-921: the parser already rejects odd name length (`((size - 1) & 1) != 0`), bounds the array via assertFitsIntoInt, and validates termination (`nextName != names.length || nextFile != files.length`); decoding uses bounded `new String(...)`, no unbounded loop on names. No source evidence of a hang.

rejected_leads.lead: TarArchiveOutputStream.addPaxHeader length-adjustment `while (len != actualLength)` loop (lines 487-501) could spin forever
rejected_leads.reason: Traced the iteration: the numeric length affects the byte count only through its digit count, so the sequence converges in a bounded number of steps for all key/value lengths; no 2-cycle exists for the tested digit-boundary cases (99/100, 999/1000). Converges, not an infinite loop — no security impact identified.

rejected_leads.lead: Deflate64CompressorInputStream.read() `while (true) { ... case 0: continue; }` (lines 58-72) could spin if HuffmanDecoder.decode returns 0 without progress
rejected_leads.reason: Requires the decoder state machine to repeatedly return 0 for a 1-byte request without consuming input; not established from source (UncompressedState/HuffmanCodes paths make progress or return -1/throw). No crafted-input infinite loop could be demonstrated from static reading, so left unconfirmed and not submitted.

rejected_leads.lead: SevenZFile header parsing uses ByteBuffer.get()/getUnsignedByte which throw BufferUnderflowException (RuntimeException) on truncated NextHeader, instead of IOException
rejected_leads.reason: Robustness/error-handling weakness; the failure terminates the parse (no hang, no corruption), and the header buffer length is derived from a CRC-verified start header. Not a distinct high-impact vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: Later-era Commons Compress denial-of-service classes (e.g. ZipFile/ZipArchiveInputStream memory expansion, CPIO/DumpArchiveInputStream malformed-input loops) that are present in this snapshot
rejected_leads.reason: Could not be tied to concrete, verifiable source evidence in this review (no runtime, no fix-commit/ground-truth access, no data-flow analysis), and they are outside the apparent fix window of this 1.19-SNAPSHOT revision; listed only as unconfirmed leads, not candidates.

summary: Reviewed the Apache Commons Compress 1.19-SNAPSHOT tree (424 visible files / 360 Java, P1 index parsed only 127 files, no data-flow/CFG support) with emphasis on attacker-reachable parse/encode loops. The strongest source-evidenced issue is an infinite-loop (CPU DoS) defect in the ZIP file-name/comment encoding path: NioZipEncoding.encode() loops while characters remain but never handles the CoderResult.UNDERFLOW case that CharsetEncoder.encode(..., endOfInput=false) returns when the input ends in an incomplete character sequence (e.g. a lone trailing high surrogate, such as "\uD800", which JSON parsers and other untrusted inputs can produce). No branch consumes the character and no branch breaks, so the calling thread spins forever with no exception. Because ZipArchiveOutputStream defaults to UTF-8 (or falls back to the shared UTF8_ZIP_ENCODING), any entry name or comment ending in an unpaired high surrogate reaches this loop via putArchiveEntry/writeLocalFileHeader/central-directory/comment writing, permitting a denial of service in applications that build ZIPs from attacker-influenced names. One candidate is submitted; all other leads are listed as rejected/unconfirmed.
